item.title: Exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings
item.description: arXiv:2610.22782v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We prove a criterion for detecting exotic symplectomorphisms of strong fillings of closed contact manifolds. The criterion concerns symplectomorphisms induced by free contact circle actions on the boundary, and it is expressed purely in topological terms. As an application, we show that one-point blow-ups of an infinite family of Brieskorn varieties admit exotic compactly supported symplectomorphisms.
item.dc:creator: Du\v{s}an Drobnjak

item.title: Symplectic Lie groups and nilmanifolds associated with acyclic quivers
item.description: arXiv:2610.23794v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: We give combinatorial criteria for the existence of left-invariant symplectic forms on the positive and full path Lie groups of finite acyclic quivers. For the nilpotent positive path Lie groups, the criterion also determines whether their compact quotients admit symplectic forms and forces the nilpotency step to be at most three. For the completely solvable full path Lie groups, we give a direct combinatorial criterion and an equivalent recursive criterion. In the symplectic case, the recursive procedure is realized by successive Hamiltonian reductions ending at an abelian symplectic Lie group. We characterize the existence of Lagrangian normal subgroups for a given form in both families, with applications to Lagrangian torus fibrations of compact nilmanifolds. We also describe the cohomology rings of the compact symplectic nilmanifolds and determine all Lefschetz ranks.
item.dc:creator: Yihao Zheng

item.title: Finite Cyclic Fundamental Groups and Exotic Universal Covers from the Cartwright--Steger Surface
item.description: arXiv:2610.23711v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We use a particular nodal curve on the Cartwright-Steger surface to construct minimal symplectic four-manifolds with arbitrary nontrivial finite cyclic fundamental group and fixed topological invariants $(e,\sigma,\chi_h,c_1^2)=(43,1,11,89)$. Using these symplectic four-manifolds as building blocks, we construct a symplectic 4-manifold that is homeomorphic to $(22m-1)\mathbb{CP}^2\#(21m-1)\overline{\mathbb{CP}}^{\,2}$ for any integer $m\geq 2$.
item.dc:creator: Anar Akhmedov, B. Doug Park, S\"{u}meyra Sakall{\i}, Sai-Kee Yeung

item.title: Conformally symplectic structures and the Lefschetz condition
item.description: arXiv:2403.12304v3 Announce Type: replace Abstract: This short note provides a symplectic analogue of Vaisman's theorem in complex geometry. Namely, for any compact symplectic manifold satisfying the hard Lefschetz condition in degree 1, every locally conformally symplectic structure is in fact globally conformally symplectic, whenever there is a mutually compatible almost complex structure.
item.dc:creator: Mehdi Lejmi, Scott O. Wilson

item.title: A Multidimensional Birkhoff Theorem for some $C^0$ Lagrangians
item.description: arXiv:2609.28373v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: We prove a multidimensional Birkhoff theorem for a new class of "$C^0$ Lagrangian subsets" in cotangent bundles, obtained as Hausdorff limits of compact exact Lagrangian submanifolds with control on their Liouville primitives. If the successive images of such a subset $L$ under the flow of a Tonelli Hamiltonian admit convergent subsequences in both positive and negative time, then $L$ and all its images are Lipschitz graphs over the base. This extends Birkhoff's celebrated theorem for twist maps of the annulus and its known higher-dimensional generalizations, and provides a first version of such results for merely continuous objects. The proof combines Floer-theoretic graph selectors, variational solutions of the Hamilton-Jacobi equation, and weak KAM theory. We also investigate the rigidity and uniqueness of limiting primitives for this new class of singular Lagrangian subsets, which may be of independent interest in $C^0$ symplectic topology.
item.dc:creator: Skander Charfi, Ibrahim Trifa

item.title: Localization of Lagrangian Floer homology for $\mathbb{Z}_p$-actions
item.description: arXiv:2610.14468v2 Announce Type: replace Abstract: For an odd prime $p$, we prove a Smith inequality over $\mathbb{F}_p$ for exact Lagrangian Floer homology under a symplectic $\mathbb{Z}_p$-action, assuming an equivariant stable normal trivialization compatible with the Lagrangians and the required relative Pin data. As an application, we obtain a rank inequality between the symplectic Khovanov homology of a $p$-periodic link and that of its quotient. These results extend the involutive localization of Seidel and Smith. The main construction is a stabilized chain complex. At every invariant intersection point we adjoin the Morse complex of a finite-dimensional normal spectral sphere, whose generators lie in free $\mathbb{Z}_p$-orbits. The differential counts holomorphic strips coupled to sphere half-trajectories by a one-sided weighted asymptotic evaluation. We prove transversality, a uniform spectral cutoff, and the compactification and gluing statements needed for the chain identity. The stabilized complex is quasi-isomorphic to the ordinary Floer complex and contains the complex of the fixed data as a subcomplex with free quotient, so the algebraic Smith inequality applies.
item.dc:creator: Erkao Bao, Tyler Lawson, Cheuk Yu Mak

item.title: Billiards and Hofer's Geometry
item.description: arXiv:2507.04767v3 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: We present a link between billiards in convex plane domains and Hofer's geometry, an area of symplectic topology. For smooth strictly convex billiard tables, we prove that the Hofer distance between the corresponding billiard ball maps admits an upper bound in terms of a simple geometric distance between the tables. We use this result to show that the billiard ball map of a convex polygon lies in the completion, with respect to Hofer's metric, of the group of smooth area-preserving maps of the annulus. Finally, we discuss related connections to dynamics and pose several open problems.
item.dc:creator: Mark Berezovik, Konstantin Kliakhandler, Yaron Ostrover, Leonid Polterovich
